Hi, I am Enhao Cheng (程恩浩) 👋

I am a Ph.D. student at Southeast University, advised by Prof. Fan Liu (刘帆).

My research interests lie in large language models and generative recommendation. My published work also explores graph clustering, short text clustering, and graph contrastive learning for recommendation.

I serve as a reviewer for ICLR, The Web Conference (WWW), and ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS).

KDD 2026Short Text Clustering

A Non-parametric Multi-view Model for Short Text Clustering

Enhao Cheng, Xiaolong Zheng, Jintong Li, Juncheng Hou, Fan Liu, Xuemeng Song, Tian Gan, Jianhua Yin

ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD), 2026

Paper ↗ Code ↗
Research summary

NMVM brings together word-count features and dense semantic embeddings in a non-parametric model for short text clustering. Two complementary mixture-model views share clustering information, allowing the model to infer the number of clusters while retaining representative words that help interpret each topic.

ACM TOIS 2026Recommendation

Prompt-Guided Graph Contrastive Learning with Controllable Augmentation and Fine-Grained Preference Modeling for Recommendation

Shoujia Zhang, Enhao Cheng, Han Liu, Jianhua Yin, Tian Gan, Xuemeng Song, Yinwei Wei, Weili Guan

ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS), 2026

Paper ↗
Research summary

PGCL uses learnable prompt nodes to represent fine-grained preferences and guide graph augmentation. Prompt-guided contrastive learning aligns users and items with relevant prompts, while interaction-enhanced contrastive learning preserves collaborative signals from observed interactions. This combines controllable augmentation with more detailed preference modeling for recommendation.

ECAI 2025Graph Clustering

Dual-Center Graph Clustering with Neighbor Distribution

Enhao Cheng, Shoujia Zhang, Jianhua Yin, Li Jin, Liqiang Nie

European Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ECAI), 2025

Paper ↗ arXiv ↗ Code ↗
Research summary

DCGC uses neighbor distributions to guide graph representation learning and select informative hard negatives. It combines feature centers with neighbor-distribution centers to form a dual-target distribution, providing complementary guidance for clustering rather than relying on a single feature-based target.

Preprint 2025Short Text Clustering

An Enhanced Model-based Approach for Short Text Clustering

Enhao Cheng, Shoujia Zhang, Jianhua Yin, Xuemeng Song, Tian Gan, Liqiang Nie

arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.13793, 2025

Paper ↗ Code ↗
Research summary

This work studies efficient mixture-model approaches to short text clustering. It improves initialization, adapts word weights using entropy, and merges clusters to refine clustering granularity. The resulting approach aims to address sparse text representations while producing interpretable topic clusters.
